what: One leaf image is multiplied to 14 and scattered around the section center at horizontal −800~500px · vertical −2 screens~0 (initial rotation 0~360°). Each leaf falls 2.6 screens straight (linear) over 20±10s. Meanwhile it sways ±120px · ±180° in a 1.5s tempo sine.inOut back-and-forth, and after landing it rests .5~1.5s and restarts from the same spot. Fall and sway tempos differ, so each leaf seems to take a different path.

options.fall · spread: Fall duration and per-leaf ± spread (s), default 20 · 10
options.drop: Falling distance (multiple of screen height) — start is −drop screens to 0, fall is drop × 1.3, default 2
options.x-min · x-max: Horizontal start position (from center, px), default −800 · 500
options.[data-fx-part=leaf]: A single leaf graphic to be called (svg or img) — hides itself. Color comes from the svg’s currentColor, set via color in the consuming css

from.where: index.html white leaves on the right preview face (original .leaf ×14 — x random(−800,500) · y random(−2·innerHeight,0) · rotation random(0,360), timeline repeat −1 · repeatDelay random(.5,1.5): y += 2.6 screens 20±10s none, x ±120 · rotation ±180 sine.inOut yoyo 1.5s × 14)

note: Even-numbered leaves use z-index 2 to pass over everything else in the section (z 1). With reduced motion, they stay at their scattered positions. The section is clipped with overflow: hidden. The CSS-only form that attaches one leaf at a time is leaf-fall-sway.
